Patronize

PAY-truh-nyz · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To patronize is to talk down to someone in a way that seems kind but actually shows a lack of respect for their intelligence or ability.

The tech support agent's tendency to patronize older customers, chirping 'good job!' after every single click as though praising a toddler, generated constant complaints.

Worked Example

Rather than answering the new intern's question directly, the manager patronized her with a slow, over-explained answer clearly meant for someone far less capable.

To patronize someone is to disguise disrespect as helpfulness -- the tone sounds sweet, but the message underneath is 'I don't think you can handle this.'

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

condescend: to talk to someone as if they were beneath you (a word taught elsewhere in this course)

belittle: to make someone seem less important (a word you'll also meet in this unit)

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

respect: to hold someone in high regard

empower: to give someone confidence or ability

Where it sits · how much disrespect comes through — oversimplify → patronize → demean

oversimplify vs. patronize: To oversimplify is just to explain something in an overly basic way -- it doesn't necessarily carry patronize's undertone of fake kindness.

demean vs. patronize: Demean goes further than patronize, openly lowering someone's dignity rather than hiding the disrespect behind a sweet tone.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — patron

Root — patron: protector, patron -- a 'father figure' (from Latin patronus, 'protector,' from pater, 'father')

Suffix — -ize

Suffix — -ize: to make or treat as (Greek -izein)

Put it together

Put it together: Patronize combines patron ('protector,' from Latin patronus, itself from pater, 'father') with -ize ('to treat as'). To patronize someone now means to treat them the way an overbearing 'father figure' might -- with a fake kindness that's really just condescension.

Use the root in a new word: paternal

Use the root in a new word: paternal: Paternal describes something fatherly -- from the same patr- root as patronize.

Root Check

Word Choice

Patronize is almost always about a fake or overblown kindness that hides real disrespect -- unlike this unit's disparage, which criticizes openly, patronizing someone pretends to be nice about it. (Patronize can also mean simply 'to be a regular customer of a business,' but this unit teaches only its talking-down sense.)
